alternative_hypothesis: The lagged BAA10Y change (basis points, latest available at the decision close) has a negative coefficient in the daily BAA10Y->DGS10 partial lead-lag regression (spread widening predicts lower next-day DGS10 changes, the flight-to-safety direction), with partial R-squared at least 0.005 and a positive holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared. Note on wording: the planner draft's 'positive, out-of-sample component' refers to positive incremental explanatory power (incremental R-squared above zero), not to a positive coefficient — the expected coefficient sign is negative on the economic argument in the mechanism, independently of that wording. Note also that the mechanical sign is negative too (the predictor contains minus the target's own lag-2 change by construction), which is why the baseline controls for the target's own lag-2 change — see the mechanism and the known confounders.
benchmark: Own-history baseline: next-day DGS10 change predicted from its own lagged change (lag 1), its own lag-2 change (the mechanical guard) and the SPX common-factor control only, without the lagged BAA10Y change
cost_assumptions: DGS10 is a yield and is not directly tradable. Tradable proxies exist — 10-year Treasury futures (ZN) and Treasury ETFs (IEF) — and free price series exist for both on Yahoo (ZN=F returned 24 closes in the last month, last close 105.671875, verified 2026-11-19 via the query2 chart endpoint; IEF likewise). But converting a yield-change signal into a futures or ETF position requires a DV01/duration conversion and, for futures, roll handling across quarterly contract rolls — a modelling layer this study does not preregister or validate, so no clean cost measurement is available from the proxy series.
The cost gate is therefore informational, not a verdict criterion; the holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared carries the economic weight
The reported gross sign-rule edge applies no costs at all, is measured in basis points per day on the DGS10 change itself, and is an upper bound on any tradable edge
cost_model: Informational only (study 003's precedent for a non-tradable target): DGS10 is a yield and is not directly tradable. Free proxy price series exist (Yahoo ZN=F and IEF both return data, verified 2026-11-19), but converting a yield-change signal into a futures or ETF position requires a DV01/duration conversion and futures roll handling that this study does not model, so no clean cost measurement is available. The trial reports the gross sign-rule edge on holdout out-of-sample augmented forecasts (1x, always invested while positioned, no costs applied, in basis points per day) as an informational upper bound on any tradable edge, with a block-bootstrap confidence interval; the holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared carries the economic weight. The cost gate is not a verdict criterion.
design_note: Researcher decisions beyond the planner draft (rank 1, credit-baa-10y-spread__rates-us-10y-yield): (1) the predictor is the daily LEVEL change of the spread in basis points, not the log return the draft's target_definition names — a spread quoted in percentage points has no meaningful log return (same correction as studies 008/009/010/011); (2) the target is the daily LEVEL change of DGS10 in basis points, not the log return the draft names — a yield quoted in percentage points has no meaningful log return either (a new correction: in study 011 the target's log change was correct because VXN is an index level; here both legs are yields); (3) the universe adds index:sp500 as the common-factor control leg — the draft's research question assumes a common-factor control but names none, and the lab convention (studies 001/003/008/010/011) is a third-asset control in the primary test; it also adds credit:baa-yield (FRED BAA, the Moody's Baa corporate bond yield) as a fourth leg, used only for the decomposition check — the supplementary regression with the lagged BAA change as the predictor, which tests the non-mechanical component directly; (4) the baseline controls for the target's own lag-2 change in addition to its lag-1 change: BAA10Y is defined as the BAA yield minus DGS10, so the lag-2 predictor contains minus the target's own lag-2 change by construction, and if DGS10 changes are autocorrelated the predictor could 'predict' the target purely mechanically — the lag-2 control blocks that channel (it is PIT-clean: DGS10 posts on the next business day, study 007 N=1, so the change ending at t-2 is available at the decision close). The lag-2 control is a mechanical guard, not a factor control: it is retained in the no-factor upper bound, where 'no-factor' means no SPX, not no guard; (5) the control uses control_lag_steps=0 (the SPX log change over day t, SPX[t]): Yahoo posts the close the same evening, so it is knowable at the decision close — per the study-007 publication-lag module, Yahoo market data carries no posting lag and is not shifted; (6) the BAA10Y predictor is lagged 2 trading days by availability (see the publication-lag note in the README), so the effective predictor for the change over t+1 is the change ending at t-2 — this is a lag-2 predictor by value date, deliberately, and the report says so; (7) the cost gate is informational, not a verdict criterion, following study 003's precedent for a non-tradable target — the verdict therefore has three criteria, not four. Note on the proxy check: free ZN futures and IEF price series DO exist on Yahoo (verified 2026-11-19); the informational treatment rests on the DV01/roll modelling gap, not on missing data — the design does not claim otherwise; (8) the sample is the full window (2003-01-02 to the fetch date): DGS10 is still published — the windows follow study 008/010/011 (train to 2020, validation to 2024, holdout 2024 to the fetch date). V2 AMENDMENT (pre-trial, before any trial ran): v1 assumed a daily FRED BAA series for the decomposition leg; the fetch showed FRED publishes BAA monthly only (286 rows, 2003-01 to 2026-10, verified from the raw CSV payload), so no daily BAA series exists to fetch. V2 drops the BAA fetch leg from the universe and derives the daily BAA change from the identity ΔBAA = ΔBAA10Y + ΔDGS10 instead. Given the lag-2 guard, the lagged-ΔBAA supplementary regression is a restatement of the primary test (the ΔDGS10 component of the derived predictor is already controlled), not independent evidence — it is reported as a decomposition consistency check. Nothing else changes: the predictor, target, guard, control, verdict criteria and windows are identical to v1. The amendment was discovered during the fetch (pre-trial data contact: coverage checks and the lag verification are the only pre-trial data contact allowed) and registered before any result was examined.
exclusions: Bars outside the sample window (2003-01-02 to 2026-11-19) are out of sample; the panel ends where the data ends (the FRED legs bind, one trading day behind the fetch date).
Incomplete synchronized rows are excluded and counted.
FRED empty-field missing values are excluded at fetch time and counted.
The first two panel return rows have no lagged BAA10Y change and are dropped.

The naive unlagged alignment, the no-factor control, the reverse placebo, the sub-period stability split and the decomposition checks (predictor-guard correlation, lagged-BAA supplementary regression with the BAA change derived from the identity ΔBAA = ΔBAA10Y + ΔDGS10, DGS10 change autocorrelations) are descriptive only and are not in the test family.
known_confounders: MECHANICAL CONFOUND (the core design issue, same class as E0026's caveat): BAA10Y is defined as the BAA yield minus the 10-year Treasury yield (DGS10), so the lag-2 predictor contains minus the target's own lag-2 change by construction: ΔBAA10Y(t-2) = ΔBAA(t-2) - ΔDGS10(t-2). If DGS10 changes are autocorrelated, the predictor could 'predict' the target purely mechanically, and the mechanical sign is negative — the same as the economic (flight-to-safety) sign — so the two cannot be told apart without a guard. The baseline therefore controls for the target's own lag-2 change ΔDGS10(t-2) in addition to its lag-1 change; that control is PIT-clean (DGS10 posts on the next business day, study 007 N=1, so the change ending at t-2 is available at the decision close). After the guard, the predictor's incremental information comes essentially from the ΔBAA(t-2) component. The decomposition checks (predictor-guard correlation; the lagged-ΔBAA supplementary regression, with the daily BAA change derived from the identity ΔBAA = ΔBAA10Y + ΔDGS10 because FRED publishes BAA monthly only — see the v2 amendment note; DGS10 change autocorrelations) quantify the mechanical component and are reported alongside the primary result. Whatever the verdict, the result must not be presented as clean transmission evidence without this caveat.

The reverse placebo (DGS10->BAA10Y) is itself mechanically confounded: its target BAA10Y contains minus DGS10, so a lagged DGS10 change could 'predict' the next-day BAA10Y change through the target's own construction if DGS10 changes are autocorrelated. It is descriptive only and its interpretation must carry the caveat.

The 2-trading-day BAA10Y availability lag is verified behaviorally (6b evidence probe 2026-11-18T21:45Z plus the fetch-time re-check) and assumed constant across the sample. If the historical posting lag differed, the predictor alignment is wrong for those periods.
FRED series are revised over time; the fetch records the current vintage. Historical values as first published may differ from the current vintage (revision risk is unmodelled).

The own-history baseline uses the DGS10 change over day t (lag 1) as a predictor for the change over t+1. Under the study's source-based PIT convention (FRED posts day-t values the next business day), the day-t DGS10 value is published the next morning, so the baseline uses information the FRED source had not yet published at the decision close. The same convention was used in studies 003, 009, 010 and 011. It strengthens the baseline against the source, so the incremental test is conservative: the source must beat a baseline that already knows the target's most recent change. The lag-2 guard control is different: it is PIT-clean (see the first confounder), and the two must not be conflated.

The SPX control is the log change over day t (SPX[t], study 003's factor-alignment precedent): Yahoo posts the close the same evening, so it is knowable at the decision close. It absorbs the day-t common equity shock by design — that is what a same-day control is for.
The sample covers the 2008 crisis, the 2020 COVID crash and the 2022 rate shock; transmission may be regime-dependent. Sub-period stability is descriptive only.

DGS10 changes are close to unpredictable (study 003's base-model R-squared for next-day VIX log changes was about 0.012, and rates changes are similarly close to a random walk); the baseline explains little, so the incremental R-squared is measured against a weak baseline.

The PIT store records available_at equal to the event time (adapter limitation); the publication lag is enforced in the trial's panel construction via the study-007 lagged-changes module, not in the stored observations.
mechanism: A widening BAA credit spread reflects rising credit risk premia and tightening financial conditions: corporate funding costs rise relative to Treasuries as default risk is repriced. The same risk-off impulse drives flight-to-safety flows into Treasuries, pushing Treasury prices up and yields down — so a widening spread should predict a falling 10-year yield the next trading day. The expected sign is negative: spread widening predicts lower next-day DGS10 changes. The spread is an end-of-day published signal, so any transmission should appear the next trading day. Caveat, stated here because it shapes the design: the predictor contains minus the target's own lag-2 change by construction (BAA10Y = BAA yield - DGS10), and the mechanical sign is negative too — the same as the economic sign. The design therefore controls for the target's own lag-2 change in the baseline (a PIT-clean mechanical guard) and reports decomposition checks, so that a negative coefficient cannot be read as transmission when it is only arithmetic.
missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count. FRED empty-field missing values are excluded at fetch time and counted.
model_definition: Partial lead-lag OLS with Newey-West HAC standard errors (daily lagged BAA10Y change -> next-day DGS10 change); the baseline controls for the target's own lag-1 change, the target's own lag-2 change (the mechanical guard) and the SPX common-factor control
Purged walk-forward out-of-sample evaluation of the primary model (baseline: own history plus guard plus SPX control; augmented: plus lagged BAA10Y change)
Naive lead-lag scan (lags 0-5, raw Pearson correlations) as a descriptive upper bound (not in the test family)

Descriptive only: unlagged (naive) alignment, no-factor upper-bound control (the lag-2 guard is retained — 'no-factor' means no SPX, not no guard), reverse placebo (DGS10->BAA10Y, itself mechanically confounded — see known confounders), sub-period stability, decomposition checks (predictor-guard correlation, lagged-BAA supplementary regression with the BAA change derived from the identity ΔBAA = ΔBAA10Y + ΔDGS10 — a restatement of the primary test given the guard, not independent evidence — DGS10 change autocorrelations)

Cost gate is informational only (study 003's precedent): the gross sign-rule edge on holdout out-of-sample augmented forecasts, no costs applied, in basis points per day, with a block-bootstrap confidence interval — not a verdict criterion
multiple_testing_family: Credit-spread transmission to Treasury yields (1 test: daily lagged BAA10Y change -> next-day DGS10 change)
null_hypothesis: Lagged BAA10Y changes have no incremental predictive value for next-day DGS10 changes over DGS10's own history (lag-1 and lag-2 changes, the latter a mechanical guard) and the SPX common-factor control, with dependence controls.
primary_metric: Partial R-squared of the lagged BAA10Y change (bp, latest available at the decision close) in the daily BAA10Y->DGS10 partial lead-lag regression
purge_gap_note: The purge gap equals the horizon (the minimum the validator allows). Raise it if the design needs a longer embargo; never lower it.
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted primary p-value at or above 0.05
Holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared at or below 0
research_question: Does the most recent BAA10Y credit-spread change available at the close predict the next-day DGS10 change beyond DGS10's own history (including the lag-2 mechanical guard) and the SPX common-factor control?
target_definition: Next-day DGS10 level change in basis points (FRED DGS10, market yield on US Treasury securities at 10 years); the predictor is the most recent BAA10Y level change in basis points available at the decision close — under the verified 2-trading-day BAA10Y posting lag, the change ending two trading days before the decision close.
title: Credit-spread changes lead 10-year Treasury yields (DGS10)
